A Democratic win could lead to increased scrutiny of current trade policies, including tariffs and government spending. articles.summary: In a legal victory, Gina Behny has maintained ownership of her house after a dispute with her ex-partner's brother, Terry Curella. Purchasing the home in 1999 with help from her grandparents, Behny's extensive investments over 25 years were key. The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court's ruling, noting Behny's substantial financial input against Curella's slight involvement, alongside an order for Curella to pay Behny for incurred losses.

This decision overturned a previous reduction of a $37 million jury award to just $2 million. Their son, who succumbed to stage-four Burkitt lymphoma, faced complications during his treatment. The court recognized the parents as distinct entities under state law, enabling them to seek higher restitution.

articles.title: Damaged da Vinci-linked painting bought for $1,175 in 2005 sold for $450m
articles.summary: In 2005, art dealers acquired Salvator Mundi for just $1,175, initially attributing it to an artist from Leonardo da Vinci's circle. After extensive restoration and research, the painting was presented as a work by Leonardo in 2011. Its value soared dramatically, culminating in a record auction price of $450.3 million in 2017. The painting's current location remains uncertain, with reports suggesting it is stored in a secure vault in Geneva.

articles.title: How Bloomberg’s $1.8B gift helped Johns Hopkins offer free tuition to students
articles.summary: Johns Hopkins University has introduced an expansion of financial aid for eligible undergraduate students. Families with annual incomes up to $200,000 can access tuition-free education starting from 2026. In addition, families earning up to $100,000 receive funding for fees and living expenses. This expansion builds on Michael Bloomberg's substantial donation, which enabled need-blind admissions and replaced loans with grants.

articles.title: Why some hugs stay with us for years, according to study of 15,000 adults
articles.summary: A newly released study explored the emotional power of hugs and how they shape our memories. By surveying over 15,000 adults, researchers found that feelings of comfort, support, and connection heavily influenced these memories. The analysis revealed interesting gender differences in remembering hugs, highlighting that individuals with high empathy recalled emotionally significant experiences more vividly. Additionally, personal attachment styles played a role in how people viewed their memorable hugging moments.

Strategies such as providing visual reminders and making tasks more engaging can significantly help enhance their memory. Additionally, encouraging children to think ahead can promote greater responsibility in completing tasks.
